title: Emerging Profit-Pool Materiality Candidate
purpose: Test whether hub-first opportunities are higher quality when the associated economic change creates a newly material profit pool inside a company, rather than merely confirming an already-known sector or cycle.

definition.knownCycleGettingBetter: The company already participates in a widely followed profit pool and the new hub item primarily confirms magnitude, persistence, or another good datapoint.
definition.emergingProfitPoolBecomingMaterial: A previously small, under-modeled, or non-core earnings stream is accelerating enough that its contribution to consolidated earnings, cash flow, or valuation relevance may change materially.

preOutcomeQuestions: Was the profit stream already a central sell-side/company narrative before the hub event?
Was the segment/product/customer contribution previously small or non-core relative to consolidated earnings?
Does the new event increase the segment's likely contribution enough to alter consolidated earnings sensitivity?
Is there contemporaneous company evidence of order/revenue/margin conversion?
Is the consolidated valuation/price still largely anchored to the old business mix rather than the emerging profit pool?
rules: This label is a research/ranking feature only; it is not a hard gate.
Do not infer materiality from later stock returns.
Do not promote an emerging pool without direct company evidence.
Do not reject a known cycle automatically; compare quality on untouched samples.

validationPlan.reason: 2017Q4 has prior repository experiments; Q1-Q3 are kept separate as the external holdout.
validationPlan.adoptionRequirement: Replicate on at least two untouched windows before changing the production Skill.
